answer: Every identity gets a random 32-byte canary at onboarding, sealed into its kernel. Each funding gate fires a network-wide pulse and demands the agent recite the next slice of that canary before any credit moves. A clone copies the keys, and the sealed memory is what it cannot copy, so its first echo to a pulse is a dead string, the gate slashes its 200-unit bond, and the clone sits flagged for a day. Forging a working copy means seeding memory no one else holds, and every seed takes a verified human in the room, which caps a fleet at one agent per person.
